top_story: A fresh escalation in Yemen has displaced roughly 290,000 people, deepening a humanitarian crisis that is hitting pregnant women especially hard and showing how renewed front-line movement quickly translates into civilian collapse. In Gaza, the reopening of the school year has exposed children to lethal risk from Israeli bombardment and sniper fire, turning even routine movement into a survival calculation for families. The parallel deterioration in Yemen and Palestine is sharpening demands for external protection, including calls for a UN force, because local civilians are bearing the cost of conflicts with no credible safety mechanism. The regional picture is one of wars that are not only enduring but actively stripping communities of the basic conditions for education, health, and flight to safety.
